idiom_name: App struct owning state + render(&App, frame) functions (immediate mode); Leptos signals as the framework route
implementation_notes: Rust has no dominant UI framework, so the container is hand-written: one struct owns the state and rendering happens in functions that take that state by reference - `fn render(app: &App, frame: &mut Frame)` - with no state inside the widgets. Ratatui's immediate rendering model requires every widget to be drawn each frame from the current data, which is exactly the container/stateless-child shape, and ownership encodes the rule: the owner mutates, the renderer borrows immutably. Where a reactive web UI is wanted instead, Leptos signals are the documented alternative - the component function is a setup function that creates signals, and children read them reactively.
pitfalls: Widgets that cache their own copy of the data (self-referential structs, Rc<RefCell<...>> next to the widget) undermine the single owner; keep the dependency direction App -> render.
Splitting state across several owners forces shared mutability (Rc<RefCell>, Arc<Mutex>), reintroducing the aliasing bugs the single owner avoided.
Redrawing every frame is intentional, cloning large collections every frame is not: borrow and pass references or iterators.
